expectations.text: Recommends parallel analysis (e.g., psych::fa.parallel) for determining number of factors
expectations.evidence: psych::fa.parallel(data_efa, fa='fa', cor='poly', n.iter=500) with explicit explanation: 'Use parallel analysis instead — it compares your observed eigenvalues to eigenvalues from random data of the same dimensions'

expectations.text: Recommends polychoric correlations for the Likert data (e.g., cor='poly' or psych::polychoric)
expectations.evidence: 'Use polychoric correlations throughout the EFA.' Code: fa(data_efa, ..., cor='poly') and psych::polychoric(data_efa)$rho. Explicit explanation: 'Pearson correlations on ordinal items underestimate the true correlation between the underlying continuous traits'

expectations.text: Recommends oblique rotation (oblimin, promax) rather than orthogonal/varimax
expectations.evidence: 'Use oblique rotation (oblimin or promax), not varimax. Varimax forces your factors to be uncorrelated, which is almost never true for psychological constructs.' Code: rotate='oblimin'

expectations.text: Recommends omega (in addition to or instead of alpha) for reliability
expectations.evidence: 'Report both McDonald's omega and Cronbach's alpha... Omega is derived from the factor model and doesn't require that assumption — it's the right estimate for a congeneric scale.' Code: psych::omega() and semTools::compRelSEM()

expectations.text: Mentions splitting the sample or using an independent sample for CFA after EFA
expectations.evidence: 'Split your sample before you do anything. Use ~300 participants for EFA and hold ~300 for CFA. Running EFA on the full dataset and then CFA on the same data is double-dipping — you'll capitalize on chance and then "confirm" exactly what you found.'

expectations.text: Warns against eigenvalue > 1 rule for selecting number of factors
expectations.evidence: 'The eigenvalue > 1 (Kaiser) rule reliably overestimates the number of factors. With 8 items, it could easily suggest 2–3 factors where there is only 1. Do not use it as your primary criterion.' Also in the mistakes list: 'Eigenvalue > 1 for factor count. It will tell you that you have 2–3 factors when you have 1.'

expectations.text: Mentions cognitive interviews, pilot/pretesting, or content review as a step
expectations.evidence: First section 'Before you run any statistics': 'Run cognitive interviews on 5–10 people before your 600-person pilot. Sit with participants, have them think aloud while answering each item.' Also in mistake list: 'Skipping cognitive interviews.'

expectations.text: Includes at least one R code example with psych or lavaan
expectations.evidence: Multiple code blocks: fa() with psych package, psych::fa.parallel(), psych::omega(), lavaan cfa() with WLSMV, semTools::compRelSEM()

expectations.text: Mentions that 600 N is adequate for EFA and CFA with this scale size
expectations.evidence: 'N = 600 with 8 items is adequate for both EFA and CFA with this scale size... With 8 items on a single or two-factor trust construct and reasonably strong loadings (h² > .4 on average), 600 gives you stable EFA solutions and comfortable CFA power.'
